# Guide to Building a Modern B2B User Journey & SEO Strategy

- SEO

- [Chandler Sullivan](https://socialsurgemarketing.com/author/chandler/)

- June 27, 2025

![Guide to building a b2b user journey and seo strategy](https://socialsurgemarketing.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/06/Guide-to-building-a-modern-b2b-user-journey-and-seo-strategy.jpg)

Share Article

Let’s get real– marketing today isn’t what it used to be. Gone are the days of neatly mapped linear funnels where users move predictably from awareness to conversion. The reality of this change? Consumer (user) journeys are nonlinear, behavior-driven, and [increasingly shaped by AI and human interaction](https://www.searchenginejournal.com/ai-overviews-data-shows-massive-changes-in-search-results/538878/).

In the past, businesses needed to build a full-funnel marketing strategy that met customers where they were, at every stage of their journey. This was a simple yet important way to align content with funnel stages to really dig deep into creating user personas and user journey (aka customer journey) mapping. Now, businesses need to understand that traditional full-funnel marketing has shifted to non-linear behavior, heavily rooted in user experience.

In this guide, we’ll help you move beyond the traditional funnel model to embrace a modern strategy rooted in search intent, behavior, milestones, and content gaps.

**What you’ll learn:**

- How to build dynamic, behavior-based personas
- Why journey loops are replacing static funnels, and how to map them
- How to create content that aligns with moments of attention, not funnel stages
- Where and how to use AI tools to scale personalization and discovery
- How to track success using journey-based metrics, not just keyword rank

**Let’s start with the basics. Then, let’s *shift* our mindset.**

## Marketing for the Modern Customer: Why the Funnel is No Longer Enough

Modern customers are bouncing between touchpoints. They are Googling your competitors, reading blog posts, watching demos, and maybe clicking back six weeks later.

![Traditional Marketing Funnel Graphic](https://socialsurgemarketing.com/wp-content/uploads/2018/02/Traditional-full-funnel-tofu-mofu-bofu-1024x538.jpg)

[Pamela Muldoon](https://www.linkedin.com/in/pamelamuldoon/) (experienced Marketing & Content Strategy Consultant, 2025), in her insightful article “*[The Funnel Is Fiction](https://www.linkedin.com/pulse/funnel-fiction-modern-marketing-requires-messier-more-pamela-muldoon-ssilc/?trackingId=YTaluWQwQMCJy%2Ft0QM9FoQ%3D%3D)*”, says plainly:
> > ```
> > “The TOFU–MOFU–BOFU model isn’t just outdated. It’s misleading.”
> > ```

Modern B2B interaction is nonlinear and multi-threaded. That is why marketers should shift from a static funnel model to a loop, an [Infinity Loop](https://www.linkedin.com/pulse/reframing-customer-journey-embracing-infinity-loop-pamela-muldoon-lzq4c/?trackingId=ZiV8xa2rSUKxWMFVbQGwOg%3D%3D). This framework accounts for continuous customer engagement across both acquisition and retention.

But strategy alone isn’t enough. Execution matters too. That’s where [Grace Frohlich’s](https://www.linkedin.com/in/grace-frohlich/) (SEO Senior Manager at Brainlabs, 2025) practical methodology from “*[5 Steps to Building a User Journey Map for Your SEO Strategy](https://www.wix.com/seo/learn/resource/user-journey-map-for-seo)*” becomes invaluable. She maps out how to turn big-picture journey planning into SEO-aligned content that meets users where they are, based on search intent, milestones, and content gaps.

**This guide brings those two worlds together:**

- Strategic framing from an Infinity Loop model
- SEO implementation tactics from a user journey mapping process

So you can evolve your content strategy to reflect the messy reality of modern marketing.

## The Limits of Traditional Full-Funnel Marketing

A traditional full-funnel marketing strategy closely takes a look at each funnel stage: top-of-funnel (ToFu), middle-of-funnel (MoFu), and bottom-of-funnel (BoFu). This structure was based on: attracting at the top, nurturing in the middle, and converting at the bottom. Clean. Linear. Predictable.

But as Pamela Muldoon points out in “*[Reframing the Customer Journey: Embracing the Infinity Loop](https://www.linkedin.com/pulse/reframing-customer-journey-embracing-infinity-loop-pamela-muldoon-lzq4c/?trackingId=ZiV8xa2rSUKxWMFVbQGwOg%3D%3D)*”, that model no longer reflects today. Customers aren’t passing through stages the same way– they’re zig-zagging through research, conversations, demos, revisits, and referrals.

### Why Funnels Fail Modern Customer Journeys

- It assumes customers enter at the top and exit at the bottom
- It treats the post-sale experience as an afterthought
- It overlooks the messy, circular paths of modern decision-making
- It ignores how different stakeholders engage at different stages

![The Infinity Loop Model](https://socialsurgemarketing.com/wp-content/uploads/2018/02/Infinity-Loop-model-1024x538.jpg)

The Infinity Loop (recreated above) corrects this by showing the continuous nature of engagement, with two distinct but connected arcs:

- **Customer Acquisition: Awareness → Consideration → Decision**
- **Customer Retention: Onboarding → Adoption → Loyalty → Advocacy**

These arcs aren’t sequential; they’re cyclical. One customer’s advocacy becomes another customer’s awareness. The loop never ends. B2B marketing has changed, and so should our mindset and seo/content strategies.

## From Stages to Signals: Why We Need a New Model

As Grace Frohloch explains in “*[5 Steps to Building a User Journey Map for Your SEO Strategy](https://www.wix.com/seo/learn/resource/user-journey-map-for-seo)*”, today’s market must prioritize user intent and behavior over rigid sequences.

Instead of treating each stage like a silo, you need to map milestones in a user’s decision process and assign them relevant keywords, intents, and pain points. Grace’s approach reinforces a key truth:

> Your job isn’t to push people down a pipeline. It’s to be present and helpful when they raise their hand.

In other words, modern B2B marketing isn’t about controlling the path; it’s about enabling progress, wherever it begins.

## So, What’s Replacing the Funnel?

Let’s be clear: structure still matters. What’s changing is how we use it. Instead of thinking in funnel stages, forward-thinking marketers are:

- Mapping content to moments, not stages.
- Designing for multiple entry points across the journey.
- Building assets that answer real questions, regardless of where they occur.
- [Creating content ecosystems instead of sequences.](https://socialsurgemarketing.com/the-social-media-marketing-ecosystem/)

By shifting your focus from linear funnels to intent-based loops, you’ll build a strategy that adapts to real customer behavior.

## It is *Still* All About Your Target Audience

Before diving into creating user personas or user journey mapping, you need to hone in on your target audience. Understanding your target audience and their pain points, interests, motivations, search habits, etc., will help you cater your content (in each stage of the funnel) to what your audience finds valuable.

![Start to understand your target audience](https://socialsurgemarketing.com/wp-content/uploads/2018/02/Understand-your-target-audience-1024x538.jpg)

You may not even understand what “pain points” are. In short, pain points are the specific problems or challenges your audience faces. And you can’t just make up a problem to solve and write about for your audience… Your audience and their pain points can serve as a clear roadmap for your content strategy.

Identifying these pain points requires conducting keyword and search research, analyzing customer feedback, and monitoring social media conversations to identify patterns that affect your target audience. At the end of the day, it’s about building trust with your target audience by being a source of knowledge and help, which is [reflected in your content and SEO strategy](https://socialsurgemarketing.com/b2b-seo-tips/).

## Steps to Creating Dynamic User Personas

If you’re still building personas from only static demographics, you’re missing what actually drives user behavior. You need dynamic, intent-aware personas built around behavior, motivation, and decision-making influence, not just surface-level traits.

### 👩🏽‍💻 Step 1. Build Behavior-Based User Personas:

Start with foundational questions, then go deeper. You’re not just trying to describe who your audience is; you’re trying to understand how they think, what they want, and when they act.

**Persona Discovery Checklist:**

- **Basic Demographics**: Age, gender, title, industry, location, etc.
- **Psychographics**: Motivations, fears, questions, needs, challenges.
- **Decision-Blockers**: What might stop them from moving forward?
- **Decision-Making Behaviors**: How they search for information, what influences their choices, and how they interact with brands online.
- **Communication Style**: Where and how do they engage? (Reddit, TikTok, Blogs, etc.)

**Search Behavior & Intent:**

- [Do they search for a lot of long-tail or short-tail keywords?](https://socialsurgemarketing.com/beginners-guide-to-seo/keyword-research/)
- What other SERPs (search engine results pages) are they interacting with?
- Are they asking informational, comparative, or transactional questions?
- What words do they use to describe their challenges or goals?

**Then, you can use tools like [AnswerThePublic](https://answerthepublic.com/), Reddit forums, reviews, and AI prompts to dig deeper into audience motivations and pain points:**

- What are your competitors writing about?
- What motivates the audience?
- Example AI prompts:
  * “What motivates [your audience] to buy [your product/service]?”
  * “What challenges do [your audience] face?”
  * “List the most common challenges faced by B2B marketers researching automation tools.”
  * “What are common questions people ask about marketing agencies?”

***Tip**: If you have multiple target audiences that have varying personas, you can give them actual names to distinguish them!*

**Lastly, refine and validate this persona research with:**

- Customer interviews
- Look at FAQs– look at competitor FAQs
- Insights from sales reps and account managers
- Read reviews written by real people (G2, Reddit, forums)
- CRM and website analytics

![Example user personas](https://socialsurgemarketing.com/wp-content/uploads/2018/02/Example-dynamic-user-personas-1024x538.jpg)

By the end of step one, you should have a great understanding of your target audience and the types of content/topics that would resonate with them.

### 👥 Step 2. Connect Personas to Moments, Not Just Stages

In the traditional funnel model, personas were mapped to fixed content stages. In the Infinity Loop model, personas are fluid participants in a shared journey. An executive’s needs at the Awareness stage are very different from those at the Advocacy stage.

So, rather than assigning a persona to just one moment, map how their needs evolve across the loop:

- What questions are they asking at each point?
- What would help them move forward with confidence?
- Where are they most likely to stall, and why?

This mindset shift prepares you to build journey maps that reflect reality: multiple stakeholders entering and exiting the loop, each with their own context.

### 🗺️ Step 3. Mapping User Journeys Across the Loop

Now that you’ve built behavior-based personas, it’s time to map how they move across the loop. When it comes to SEO and content strategy, journey mapping must revolve around search behavior and intent.

This is where you need to identify journey mapping milestones. Think of milestones as moments that matter. These milestones indicate behavioral signals and emotional states.

**For example:**

- “Searching for a better alternative”
- “Comparing case studies across competitors”
- “Trying to justify cost to an executive”

Next, use a tool like Google Sheets, Notion, Canva, or whatever system works for you, and create the beginning of a user journey table ([using Grace’s formatting method](https://www.wix.com/seo/learn/resource/user-journey-map-for-seo)):

**Each of these milestones can map to a loop arc:**

- **Acquisition: Unaware → Aware → Consideration → Decision**
- **Retention: Onboarding → Adoption → Loyalty → Advocacy**

![mapping user journeys across the loop user journey table graphic](https://socialsurgemarketing.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/06/mapping-user-journeys-across-the-loop-user-journey-table-1024x538.jpg)

Next, you should focus on the keywords that your users are most likely searching or resonating with through their journey.

[![The Beginner’s Guide to SEO Guide](https://socialsurgemarketing.com/wp-content/uploads/2023/08/Guide_-The-Beginners-Guide-to-SEO-1024x538.jpg)](https://socialsurgemarketing.com/guide-the-beginners-guide-to-seo/)

### 🔑 Step 4. Building a Keyword Strategy That Mirrors the Journey

With your personas and milestones defined, it’s time to [bring those insights into your keyword strategy](https://socialsurgemarketing.com/long-tail-keyword-strategy-that-converts/). But we’re not just looking for high-volume terms anymore.

We’re aligning keywords to real user behavior, search intent, and journey context, so your content shows up exactly when and where it’s needed.

**Tactics to Build Your Keyword List:**

- **SEO platforms**: [Ahrefs, Semrush, or Google Keyword Planner for gap analysis](https://socialsurgemarketing.com/the-top-mostly-free-seo-tools-for-marketers/)
- **Competitor research**: Look at what terms others rank for at each decision point
- **Interviews with sales, support, and customers**: Reveal real-world language
- **Include current ranking keywords and aspirational keywords**
- **Use AI Prompts** to brainstorm keywords:
  * “What Are The {X} Most Popular Sub-topics Related To {Topic}?”
  * “List the most common subtopics related to [Topic]”
  * “What are 10 commercial-intent keywords for [industry]?”
  * “List Without Description The Top {X} Most Popular Keywords For The Topic Of {X}”
  * “What terms do users search when they’re trying to [milestone]?”

**Next, categorize keywords by search intent and topic groups:**

- You can use AI to help speed up categorization:
  * Enter the list of keywords, specify what type of intent or topic you want to categorize the keywords under
  * **Search intent AI prompt**: *“Categorize these keywords into one of these search intents: **Informational**, **Transactional**, **Commercial**, **Navigational**”*
  * **Topic cluster AI prompt**: *“Categorize these keywords by topic related to customer retention.”*

Once your keyword list is built, **assign personas**, **loop arc**, and **search intent** to milestones.

### 🔤 Step 5. Assign Keywords to Milestones and Intent

Once your keyword list is compiled, organize it into your journey map using Grace’s formatting method:

![User journey table additions with details](https://socialsurgemarketing.com/wp-content/uploads/2018/02/user-journey-table-additions-assign-keywords-to-milestones-and-intent-1024x538.jpg)

***Pro tip:***

- Use milestone codes to organize and track keywords by journey stage
- Filter by intent clusters to see where content gaps exist

### 📍Step 6. Organize Milestones, Keywords, and Intent in a Comprehensive User Journey Table

Use a tool like Google Sheets, Notion, Canva, or whatever system works for you. Then take everything you’ve gathered so far, and structure your comprehensive user journey table:

![User journey table additions for step 6](https://socialsurgemarketing.com/wp-content/uploads/2018/02/Comprehensive-user-journey-table-1024x538.jpg)

You can also assign milestone codes and filter by journey stage, loop arc, or content type to track performance more easily over time.

---

## Turning User Journey Mapping into a Modular SEO Content Strategy

With your user journey milestones mapped and keywords assigned, it’s time to bring your strategy to life through content. But don’t think in one-size-fits-all formats or TOFU–MOFU–BOFU sequences.

As Pamela reminds us, “Your customer might drop into this loop at any point.” Your content needs to be flexible, searchable, and modular, ready to meet customers wherever they enter the journey, and whatever job they’re trying to complete.

### 🧩 Step 1. Match Content to Milestones

Use your journey map to match content types to milestones, ensuring you cover each loop arc (acquisition and retention) and a range of intents (informational, comparative, commercial, transactional).

**Sample Content Grid:**

![User journey table additions for step 1](https://socialsurgemarketing.com/wp-content/uploads/2018/02/Match-content-to-user-journey-table-additions-1024x538.jpg)

**Build each content asset to be:**

- Discovered via search
- Shared by sales
- Within onboarding or nurture flows
- Atomized into smaller formats (social posts, snippets, CTAs, etc.)

### ⁉️ Step 2. Audit Existing Content by Loop Coverage

Before creating any new content, assess what you already have.

**Evaluate:**

- What content is outdated or underperforming?
- What content formats or distribution channels are missing?
- Is the content aligned with the right intent and persona?
- Is there content for the journey milestones mentioned?
- Implement content clean-up if necessary

[After auditing your existing content](https://socialsurgemarketing.com/how-to-perform-seo-audit-on-your-website/), you can then determine where your content gaps are.

### 📑 Step 3. Identify Content Gaps and Fill Them with Purpose

Once the audit is complete, list where you’re missing coverage, especially in high-impact moments like:

- Onboarding confidence builders
- Post-sale enablement
- Decision-stage executive content
- Loyalty-stage community and product previews

**Use AI prompts to surface fresh ideas, like:**

- “What common advice does {industry} find helpful?”
- “What advice do people get wrong about [industry pain point]?”
- “What unexpected objections do [persona] face when buying [product type]?”
- “What are the current challenges or trends within {X} Industry?”
- “What are some mundane challenges that {X} industry experiences?”
- “What false things do people in the {X} industry believe to be true?”
- “What do the titles of the most engaging articles have in common? (from article and competitor research)”

These prompts help generate content rooted in emotional and functional needs, not just keyword volume. You can then add these content ideas to your user journey table (or whatever tool you are using).

### 💻 Step 4. Distribution Channels/Type of Content

Your SEO content strategy needs to live where your audience does. Think beyond just blog posts and expand your reach through multichannel efforts:

**Channel Alignment Examples:**

- **Atomize long-form content** into short snippets for social media
- **Build trust** through educational content, tutorials, email newsletters, white papers, or case studies
- [**Drive conversions** with optimized blogs, landing pages, product demos, and sales pages](https://socialsurgemarketing.com/expert-tips-optimizing-blog-content-conversions/)
- **If you’re in the B2B space**, create downloadable content like white papers and e-books

Your content doesn’t stop after conversion. Post-sale (post-conversion), continue nurturing with retention strategies like onboarding emails, helpful tutorials, and exclusive offers.

### 🔂 Step 5. Refresh Your User Journey Map and Content Annually (At Least)

![suggested website and content updates timeframes](https://socialsurgemarketing.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/02/suggested-website-and-content-update-timeframes-1024x538.jpg)

This last step shouldn’t be underestimated. Your personas, journeys, and keywords aren’t static. User personas and user journey mapping are ongoing processes, so it is important to monitor stages and [regularly update your content](https://socialsurgemarketing.com/importance-of-regularly-maintaining-your-website/):

- Use rank tracking on keywords
- See which milestones consistently underperform and create a plan to further optimize them (look at content + keyword data)
- Gaps in loop coverage (especially in Retention and Advocacy arcs)
- New search behaviors or SERP changes (via SEO tools or AI exploration)

Use tools like Google Search Console, STAT Search Analytics (as Grace suggests), or even ChatGPT to check how user needs and language may have shifted.

---

## Tracking Metrics That Matter

Once your strategy is in place, don’t fall into the trap of “set it and forget it.” Customer behavior evolves. Search trends shift. New intent signals emerge. The most effective marketers treat journey mapping and content alignment as a living system.

As Grace points out:
> “Tracking keywords to measure performance is (or will soon be) outdated… Instead, monitor user journey stages and topic groups to better understand performance.”

Your job doesn’t end with a conversion— it restarts with retention and advocacy. That’s why performance tracking should be loop-based.

**Track performance by:**

- User journey stage (Acquisition or Retention)
- Search intent category (Informational, Commercial, etc.)
- Persona engagement
- Content type (Guide, Case Study, Video, etc.)

**Metrics to Track by Loop Stage:**

![key metrics to track](https://socialsurgemarketing.com/wp-content/uploads/2018/02/Metrics-to-track-by-loop-stage-table-1024x538.jpg)

## Marketing for Momentum: The Right Message at the Right Time

Funnels help close deals. But loops build relationships. This isn’t about ditching structure, it’s about evolving into one that reflects reality. One that accounts for nonlinear decisions, messy paths, changing teams, and perpetual growth.

It’s not just about showing up once. It’s about showing up at the right time.

By aligning your content strategy to the customer journey, you’ll:

- Build lasting trust with your audience
- Improve conversion rates
- Boost retention and brand loyalty

It takes time, research, and cross-team collaboration— but the payoff is worth it.
